Direction for questions:

A group of four friends – A, B, C and D found Rs. 20 on a table. They decided to play a game of cards to distribute the amount amongst themselves. A deck of cards was kept face down on the table. The rules of the game were as follows:

In each round each player draws one card from the pack
If a single player gets a card of the highest value amongst the four, he picks Rs. 4 from the table.
If two players get cards of the highest value, they both pick Rs. 2 from the table. If three players get cards of the highest value, each of them takes Re.1 from the fourth player (if he doesn’t have the money, he simply owes them the amount and has to pay up as soon as he earns it)
If all four players get cards of the same value, no one earns anything.
Value of the ace is the highest, followed by king, queen, etc. irrespective of the suit.
Then they proceed to the next round.
At the end of 4 rounds:
i. Each player made money in the same number of rounds.
ii. D had earned more money than anyone else and B had earned less than anyone else.
iii. There were Rs. 8 left on the table.

Which of the following is certainly True?
A and C earned Rs. 2 each in the same 	round
B had earned either Rs. 0 or Rs. 2 at the end of four rounds
had earned Rs. 2 more than C at the end of four rounds

Direction for questions:

There are certain numbers of one rupee coins and two rupee coins kept on the table. Two players play a game of picking coins in turn. The rules of the games are as follows:

(a) The players play alternately i.e. First turn for player 1 followed by player 2 and then again player 1 and so on.
(b) Each player in his turn can remove any two coins on the table on his turn but must keep back one new replacement coin as per the following rules:
i. If the coins removed are of same denominations (i.e. both one rupee OR both two rupee) then the replacement coin to be kept on the table must be a 2-rupee coin.
ii. If the coins removed are of different denominations (i.e. 1 one rupee and 1 two rupee) then the replacement coin to be kept on the table must be one rupee coin.
iii. They continue playing the game till one player can no longer follow the steps mentioned in (b). Then that person will be declared the loser and the player with the step before that is declared the winner.
Assume infinite supply of one rupee and two-rupee coins.

If the total number of coins is odd, who will win the game?

questionFeedback:
Sorry, that's not correct.
Explanation:

The transactions that can happen during the game are as follows: 
–1 – 1 + 2 = 0 (2 one rupee coin removed and a two rupee coin kept back) 
–2 – 2 + 2 = –2
1 – 2 + 1 = –2            
Thus every transaction is removing either Rs. O or Rs. 2.            
So if the initial amount is even, the final amount left on the table should also be even.            
Similarly if the initial amount is odd, the final quantity will also be odd.            
The winner is the player with the last step when there were 2 coins left on the table.            
If a player is left with just one coin then he will lose the game.            
Now if there are “n” coins on the table, it will take n – 1 transactions to reduce it to one coin (as in every transaction there is a net reduction of one coin).
Since the total number of coins is odd, number of transactions required to reach just one coin is even.
Hence second player will win the game.

Sorry, that's not correct.
Explanation:

If the coins removed are of same denomination, then replacement coin is 2 rupees            
So either it is            
–1 – 1 + 2 = 0            
or –2 – 2 + 2 = –2            
If the coins removed are of different denomination then the replacement coin is 1 rupee So it is            
1 – 2 + 1 = –2            
So whatever be the transaction the final resultant is always an even number. So if the initial amount on the table is an even number, the final amount on the table will also be even that is a 2-rupee coin, and similarly, for the initial odd amount, it will be a 1-rupee coin.            
Also in every step number of coins reduce by one coin. So if there are n coins total steps required to reduce it to just one coin is (n – 1).            
Total 1-rupee coins are even. So the total initial and final amount will be also even.
